properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 14 at 6:58PM CDT until October 14 at 8:45PM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
FFWLUB

The National Weather Service in Lubbock has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Crosby County in northwestern Texas...
Southwestern Dickens County in northwestern Texas...
Northeastern Garza County in northwestern Texas...
Northwestern Kent County in northwestern Texas...

* Until 845 PM CDT.

* At 658 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated that the heaviest rain has
ended across the warned area, but light rain will continue over the
next hour or so which will result in the continuation of flash
flooding. Between 2 and 5 inches of rain have fallen. Flash
flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
White River Lake and Kalgary.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Canadian, OK
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 14 at 6:57PM CDT until October 15 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Norman has issued a Flood Advisory
for the following rivers in Oklahoma...

North Canadian River at El Reno affecting Canadian County.

For the North Canadian River...including Woodward, Woodward, Seiling,
Watonga, El Reno, Yukon, Oklahoma City at NW 10th Street, Oklahoma
City at Britton Road, Harrah, Shawnee, Wetumka...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...North Canadian River at El Reno.

* WHEN...From this evening to Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, The river remains mostly within its banks
in Canadian County... from near El Reno to areas upstream of Yukon.
Any overbank flows affect very small agricultural areas. Low-lying
fields and private roads near the river could be briefly isolated
by flows in cutoff channels crossing the flood plain.




* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 14.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.9 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Action stage is 13.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 700 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 14 at 7:51PM EDT until October 14 at 9:15PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
At 751 PM EDT, doppler radar indicated thunderstorms had produced
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2.25 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by prior thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Parkersburg, Marietta, Harrisville, St. Marys, Vienna,
Williamstown, Pennsboro, Belmont, North Bend State Park, Boaz,
Newport, North Hills, Ellenboro, Pullman, Schultz, Willow Island,
Nutter Farm, Waverly, Maxwell and Pike.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 77 in West Virginia between mile markers 180 and 186.
Interstate 77 in Ohio between mile markers 1 and 3. Route 50 in West
Virginia between mile markers 25 and 52.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 14 at 6:49PM CDT until October 14 at 7:15PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
SVROUN

The National Weather Service in Norman has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southwestern Foard County in northern Texas...
Northwestern Knox County in northern Texas...
South central Hardeman County in northern Texas...

* Until 715 PM CDT.

* At 648 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 12 miles east of Chalk to 6 miles northwest of
Truscott, moving northeast at 40 mph.

THESE ARE DESTRUCTIVE STORMS FOR CROWELL.

HAZARD...80 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be heavily damaged. Expect
considerable damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles.
Extensive tree damage and power outages are likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Crowell and Copper Breaks State Park.
properties.instruction:
Remain alert for a possible tornado! Tornadoes can develop quickly
from severe thunderstorms. If you spot a tornado go at once into the
basement or small central room in a sturdy structure.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

This is an EXTREMELY DANGEROUS SITUATION. These storms are producing
widespread wind damage across Foard County. SEEK SHELTER NOW inside
a sturdy structure and stay away from windows!

Torrential rainfall is occurring with these storms, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 9:39AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Tropical Depression 29W continues to organize as it continues
it's long voyage towards the Marianas, and is currently located at
10.6N 160.1E, which is 1030 miles east of Guam. Movement has been
to the northwest at 13 mph, and a more gradual turn to the west-
northwest is expected. It's important for folks to keep in mind
that wobbles in the track occur all the time, and a slight change
can make a big difference in terms of who experiences what, and
for how long.

The main theme we've been telling folks is tropical storm-force
winds look probable over some locations of the Marianas between
Guam and Saipan, with typhoon conditions also possible. Heavy
rainfall will also accompany the storm. Rainfall amounts of 5 to
10 inches, with locally higher amounts possible. For our mariners,
seas will rapidly build Saturday into Sunday, with seas likely
climbing above 20 feet. Some coastal inundation is likely.

For more information on Tropical Depression 29W, please refer to
the Tropical Cyclone Public Advisory issued by the National
Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ32 PGUM and the Tropical
Cyclone Warning issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under
WMO header WTPN32 PGTW.

NWSheadline: TYPHOON CONDITIONS POSSIBLE FOR PORTIONS OF THE MARIANAS THIS WEEKEND

Northern Christian County in south central Kentucky...
Southeastern Caldwell County in western Kentucky...
Northeastern Trigg County in western Kentucky...

* WHEN...Until 930 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain

the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.

Plains and Hawkins.

properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.
